title: Runtime Experimentation Safety and Governance Checklist
author: Marina Hsu
content:
Overview

Purpose:
- Provide a practical, repeatable checklist and governance guidance for running experiments that touch the serving runtime (kernel scheduling, eviction behavior, batch shaping, quantization rollouts, routing/fallback policies, and instrumentation changes).
- Reduce risk to production SLOs and customer traffic while enabling safe iteration across runtime subsystems.

Scope:
- Applies to any change or experiment that affects: kernel selection/variants, scheduler policies, kvcache behaviour, batching/cohorting logic, fallback routing, runtime-invoked model variants, telemetry sampling strategy, and external benchmarking harnesses that mirror production traffic.
- Does NOT replace module-level ADRs or release sign-off; it complements release/runbook artifacts with gating criteria and experiment-specific guardrails.

Audience and Roles
- Experiment Owner: engineer running the experiment (responsible for checklist items, runbook, and artifact collection).
- Runtime Safety Reviewer: senior runtime engineer who approves gating thresholds and rollback criteria.
- Oncall Rotation Lead: SRE who will own paging/incident coordination if the experiment impacts production.
- Metrics Librarian: owner of benchmark & SLO dashboards who validates experiment telemetry.

Pre-experiment Proposal (required fields)
- Title and short description of the hypothesis.
- Components touched (pick from: scheduler, kernel mapper, kvcache, dispatch, routing, kv-epoch sync, telemetry pipeline).
- Risk tier (low/medium/high) — use the tier rules below.
- Target cohorts/tenants and whether experiment will touch Dedicated or Private clusters.
- Expected duration and window (start/end times).
- Safety owner and oncall paging contact.
- Rollout plan & rollback triggers (explicit thresholds).

Risk tier rules
1) Low: internal-only experiments in sandbox or staging; no production traffic and no changes to kernel binaries.
2) Medium: non-invasive production shadowing or non-stateful parameter tuning (e.g., sampling rate changes, telemetry tag additions) with canary traffic up to 1% and explicit latency/cost gates.
3) High: kernel variant rollouts, admission controller logic changes, quantization rollouts, or anything affecting multi-tenant eviction or persistent kvcache state. Requires extended approvals and a rehearsal in the experiment lab.

Preflight checklist (must be completed before start)
1) Safety doc published in the experiment backlog with owner and reviewers.
2) Experiment manifest committed to the experiment registry (example manifest snippet below).
3) Benchmarks: baseline performance and cost numbers captured from the benchmark suite for the target model and sequence-length distribution. Attach per-token latency, P99, and cost-per-1k-token.
4) Telemetry hooks: trace points, span names, and metric labels required by the profiling playbook are instrumented and reviewed. Sampling policy updated if necessary.
5) Canary cohort defined, <= 1% traffic for medium or <= 0.1% for high-risk changes initially.
6) Rollback automation tested in isolation (automated toggle that returns traffic to the previous policy or model variant).
7) Runbook authored with precise paging instructions, reproducible triage steps, and escalation contacts.
8) Owners of downstream systems (billing, analytics, deployments) notified.

Experiment manifest example (YAML)
- name: kernel-variant-hint-eta
  component: kernel-mapper
  risk_tier: high
  start_window: 2027-03-08T02:00:00Z
  duration_hours: 4
  canary_fraction: 0.001
  telemetry_required:
    - runtime/p99_latency_ms
    - runtime/error_rate_5m
    - kernel_dispatch/handoff_rate
  rollback_triggers:
    - metric: runtime/p99_latency_ms
      operator: ">"
      threshold: "+25% over baseline"
    - metric: runtime/error_rate_5m
      operator: ">="
      threshold: "0.5%"

Telemetry and profiling requirements
- Required spans and metrics (profiling-playbook alignment):
  - request.lifecycle.span (must include kernel_id, batch_size, tenant_id)
  - kernel.exec_time_ms (histogram with p50/p95/p99 buckets)
  - kvcache.miss_rate (per-tenant rolling 5m)
  - scheduler.admission_rejects (count + cause tag)
  - dispatch.queue_wait_ms (per-queue)
- Sampling: for high-risk experiments set trace sampling to 100% for canary cohort for the first hour, then 10% thereafter. Ensure traces are tagged with experiment_id and kernel_variant.
- Profiling: attach microbenchmark artifacts from the perf suite for the same model/config (binary/quantization level) used in the experiment. Include kernel-level profiles (CUDA/NVTX) and host-side wall-clock traces.

Benchmarking & gating (use the benchmarking suite)
- Minimum acceptance criteria (example):
  - End-to-end P99 increase <= 10% for low risk, <= 15% for medium, <= 5% absolute ms cap for high risk (owner must propose and safety reviewer approves).
  - Cost per token delta should be reported; for cost-first experiments set strict cost gates (e.g., cost change <= -5%).
  - Memory and GPU occupancy: no increase > 8% sustained or scheduled eviction must be disabled during the canary window.
- Shadow benchmarks: run a 30-minute synthetic replay with the production-shaped corpus and compare kernel time distributions to baseline. Attach the generated delta histogram.

Kernel scheduling and admission controller safety items
- Kernel variant selection: experiments that introduce new kernel variants must ship a compatibility whitelist. If the variant is non-deterministic under batching, flag as high-risk.
- Admission controller: any change to slot accounting or credit logic requires a simulation run using the scheduler emulator (include link to emulator run ID).
- Preemption and priority inversion: provide hypothesis and tests that show there is no new priority inversion path. Include a microburst stress test where high priority traffic is steadily increased to 2x normal for 5 minutes and confirm low-priority P50 remains below the specified cap.

Runbook (condensed)
1) Pager triage steps:
   a) Check "experiment_id" overlays in the SLO dashboard and confirm the canary cohort only.
   b) If error rate >= rollback trigger, run automated toggle to revert kernel_variant for the canary cohort (CLI: redwoodctl runtime experiment revert --id <experiment_id>).
   c) Collect top 10 traces (by latency) and attach to slack incident channel #runtime-incidents.
2) If toggle fails, scale canary down to 0 and divert traffic to fallback route: redwoodctl routing set-fallback --policy stable-default.
3) Escalation: after 4 consecutive failed toggles or if global P99 > 2x baseline, page Oncall Rotation Lead and safety reviewer.

Post-experiment artifacts and postmortem expectations
- Artifact checklist to attach to experiment entry:
  - Baseline and experiment benchmark CSVs (per-token latency, kernel time, queue time).
  - Trace bundle (ndjson) with experiment_id tag.
  - Kernel-level profiles and microbenchmark outputs.
  - Runbook timeline and any toggles applied.
  - Final decision: ship / revise / abandon with bullet justification.
- Postmortem: if experiment caused any customer-visible incident or SLO breach it requires a blameless postmortem within 3 business days with follow-ups tracked in the experiment backlog.

Known issues mapping and release notes guidance
- Any experiment that touches a subsystem with an active Known Issues entry must reference the issue ID and attach a short impact analysis.
- Release note snippet template to include in runtime release notes: "Experiment <name> ran against <component> on <date>. Result: <accept/reject>. Key signals: p99 latency delta, error delta, cost delta. Link: <experiment registry entry>."

Safe rollout patterns (recommended)
- Shadow -> Canary -> Ramp -> Hold: always run a shadow period long enough to collect representative telemetry (>= 30 minutes of production-shaped traffic) before allowing canary routing.
- Progressive kernel rollout: variant enabled for a single stable tenant first (if available), then a 0.1% multi-tenant canary, then incremental steps 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% with qualitative checks at each step.

Appendix: Operational commands & templates
- Toggle experiment (CLI): redwoodctl runtime experiment toggle --id <experiment_id> --state enable|disable
- Revert kernel variant (CLI): redwoodctl runtime kernel revert --node <node_id> --variant <variant_id>
- Collect traces (example): redwoodctl observability export-traces --experiment <id> --min-duration-ms 100 --output traces-<id>.ndjson
- Perf harness run (example): bench-suite run --profile production-shape --model <model> --seq-distribution <dist> --output bench-<id>.csv

Appendix: Quick checklist (single-line items for owners)
- [ ] Create experiment entry and manifest in registry
- [ ] Baseline benchmarks recorded and attached
- [ ] Telemetry spans/instrumentation reviewed
- [ ] Runbook and rollback automation tested
- [ ] Canary cohort scheduled and owners notified
- [ ] Oncall and safety reviewer assigned
- [ ] Shadow run completed (>=30m)
- [ ] Automated rollback exercises executed
- [ ] Post-experiment artifacts attached

Contact and escalation
- Primary safety mailbox: runtime-safety@redwood.ai
- Pager (Oncall Rotation Lead): see rota in the SRE team wiki
- Slack channels: #runtime-experiments (announce start/stop), #runtime-incidents (incident comms)

Revision history
- 2027-02-15: Initial draft by Marina Hsu
- 2027-03-02: Updated telemetry sampling guidance and added CLI snippets (reviewers: Samir Khan, Ellen Ruiz, Priya Nair)

This document is intended as a living checklist. If you are running an experiment that interacts with other spaces (dedicated, private deployments) add an explicit cross-space approval entry and notify the relevant customer owners.
